summary: Mason Lake site: a 1942 Aircraft Warning Service station, or a 1952 DNR cab per other sources; abandoned by 1961 and gone.

facts.design: Cabin: AWS station per the register; DNR cab per firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb

access.note: In 2014 Green Diamond Resources owned the land and usually allowed non-motorized access such as hiking. The access rules may have changed; check before going.

visit.trail_note: Half-mile hike from a Green Diamond gate off East Trails End Road, about 150 feet of gain, per Willhite (2014).

events.note: AWS station built per the register; Rex's page says it was activated September 11, 1942.
Mr. and Mrs. Stockman stationed at the lookout, per a June 1947 Shelton-Mason County Journal item quoted on Rex's page.
firelookout.com and Willhite date a DNR cab to 1952. The sources do not tie it to the 1942 station.
Abandoned in 1961 per the register and firelookout.com; Willhite says by 1961.

evidence.supports: AWS station built in 1942, retained by the state, lookout later abandoned
evidence.quote: An Aircraft Warning Service Station was built in 1942 and the lookout was retained by the State of Washington for fire detection.
The lookout was abandoned in 1961 and is gone.

evidence.supports: Location listed under the Washington Division of Forestry

evidence.quote: This location is said to have had a DNR cab in 1952 that was abandoned by 1961.
The current landowner in 2014 was Green Diamond Resources, who usually allow non-motorized access like hiking.

evidence.supports: Could not locate the exact spot
evidence.quote: Where the exact spot was located, I don't know but we walked all across the plateau on skid roads.

evidence.supports: Clear-cut summit gave views of the Olympics
evidence.quote: The majority of the high flat summit area had been clear-cut offering views of the entire Olympics

evidence.supports: Mount Rainier visible over the timber
evidence.quote: Even Mt. Rainier and some south Cascades were visible over the timber to the east.

evidence.supports: Route starts at East Trails End Road
evidence.quote: a left turn on East Trails End Road

evidence.supports: Route from the Green Diamond gate
evidence.quote: Follow it to the Green Diamond gate with a large pull-out

evidence.supports: Station new construction on private property
evidence.quote: was new construction built on private property by the AWS

evidence.supports: Site retained by the state after deactivation
evidence.quote: Upon the deactivation of the station, the site was retained by the State of Washington.
Mr. and Mrs. Stockman are now stationed at the Mason Lake lookout.

evidence.supports: 1947 item sourced to the Shelton-Mason County Journal

notes_for_editor: Sources conflict: the register and Rex's page tie the site to a 1942 AWS station, while firelookout.com and Willhite describe a DNR cab from 1952 and do not mention 1942. The sources do not show whether these are one structure or two, so the built event is left as the 1942 station with the 1952 cab as a separate event. The access level 'permission' is my reading of a 2014 page that says the landowner usually allows hiking; it needs a current check. Rex's page was read via its tail, so its 1944 AWS report is only quoted secondhand. A WebSearch snippet mentioned an AWS roster on WillhiteWeb; it was not read and nothing from it is used.
